from: “We are still reviewing the draft,” the lawyer said.

ok.de: Richtig: are → were: they were still reviewing, denn das Sagen liegt zurück.
ok.en: Right: are → were: they were still reviewing, because the speaking is in the past.

wrong.de: „are“ bleibt in der Gegenwart. Nach said rückt es zu were.
wrong.en: “are” stays in the present. After said it moves to were.

wrong.de: Das Schlüsselwort were muss unverändert in der Lücke stehen.
wrong.en: The key word were must stay unchanged in the gap.

from: “I haven't seen the final numbers yet,” Tom told me.
frame: Tom told me ___ the final numbers yet.

ok.de: Richtig: haven't seen → hadn't seen: Present Perfect rückt zu Past Perfect.
ok.en: Right: haven't seen → hadn't seen: present perfect moves to past perfect.

wrong.de: „hasn't seen“ bleibt in der Gegenwart. Nach told me rückt es zu hadn't seen.
wrong.en: “hasn't seen” stays in the present. After told me it moves to hadn't seen.

wrong.de: „haven't“ gehört zu I. Mit he wird daraus hadn't seen.
wrong.en: “haven't” goes with I. With he it becomes hadn't seen.

wrong.de: Das Schlüsselwort seen muss unverändert in der Lücke stehen.
wrong.en: The key word seen must stay unchanged in the gap.

prompt: He said he has been in Munich the week before.
fixed: He said he had been in Munich the week before.

ok.de: Der Fehler: has been passt nicht zu the week before. Richtig: had been.
ok.en: The error: has been does not fit the week before. Correct: had been.

wrong.de: Doch, hier ist ein Fehler: has been passt nicht zu the week before.
wrong.en: There is an error: has been does not fit the week before.

wrong.de: Der Fehler liegt bei „has been“: Nach said rückt die Zeit zurück.
wrong.en: The error is in “has been”: after said the tense moves back.

prompt: The supplier promised last year that he will deliver the parts the following week.
fixed: The supplier promised last year that he would deliver the parts the following week.

ok.de: Der Fehler: will passt nicht zu promised. Richtig: would deliver.
ok.en: The error: will does not fit promised. Correct: would deliver.

wrong.de: Doch, hier ist ein Fehler: will bleibt nicht stehen, wenn das Versprechen zurückliegt.
wrong.en: There is an error: will cannot stay when the promise lies in the past.

wrong.de: Der Fehler liegt bei „will deliver“: Das Versprechen liegt zurück, also would.
wrong.en: The error is in “will deliver”: the promise is in the past, so would.

prompt: Priya said the client had not replied, so we decided to wait.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: had not replied ist der richtige Rückschritt aus haven't replied.
ok.en: No error: had not replied is the right backshift of haven't replied.

wrong.de: Kein Fehler: Nach said steht hier korrekt das Past Perfect.
wrong.en: No error: after said the past perfect is correct here.

q.de: Welcher Satz berichtet, was sie schon früher gesagt hat?
q.en: Which sentence reports what she said some time ago?

ok.de: Richtig: Satz b. said + was zeigt, dass das Sagen zurückliegt.
ok.en: Right: sentence b. said + was shows that the speaking lies in the past.

wrong.de: In a stehen says und is: Sie sagt es jetzt, nichts rückt zurück.
wrong.en: In a, says and is: she says it now, so nothing moves back.

wrong.de: Nicht gleich: Nur b gibt eine frühere Aussage wieder.
wrong.en: Not the same: only b reports an earlier statement.

from: “The workshop starts tomorrow,” she told us.
frame: She told us the workshop would start ___.

ok.de: Richtig: tomorrow → the next day. Gezählt wird vom Sagen aus.
ok.en: Right: tomorrow → the next day. Counting starts from the speaking.

wrong.de: „tomorrow“ zählt von heute. Nach told us zählt der Tag nach dem Sagen.
wrong.en: “tomorrow” counts from today. After told us the day after the speaking counts.

wrong.de: „the day before“ zeigt zurück. would start zielt auf den Tag danach.
wrong.en: “the day before” points back. would start points to the day after.

wrong.de: Das Schlüsselwort day muss unverändert in der Lücke stehen.
wrong.en: The key word day must stay unchanged in the gap.

from: “We shipped the order yesterday,” Priya wrote.
frame: Priya wrote that they had shipped the order ___.

ok.de: Richtig: yesterday → the day before. Gezählt wird vom Schreiben aus.
ok.en: Right: yesterday → the day before. Counting starts from the writing.

wrong.de: „yesterday“ zählt von heute. Vom Schreiben aus heißt es the day before.
wrong.en: “yesterday” counts from today. From the writing it is the day before.

wrong.de: „the day after“ ist der Tag danach. Der Versand lag vor dem Schreiben.
wrong.en: “the day after” is the later day. The shipping came before the writing.

wrong.de: Das Schlüsselwort day muss unverändert in der Lücke stehen.
wrong.en: The key word day must stay unchanged in the gap.

prompt: Last year our CFO said that the new system would go live tomorrow at the Berlin site.
fixed: Last year our CFO said that the new system would go live the next day at the Berlin site.

ok.de: Der Fehler: tomorrow zählt von heute. Vom Sagen aus: the next day.
ok.en: The error: tomorrow counts from today. From the speaking: the next day.

wrong.de: Doch, hier ist ein Fehler: Die Aussage fiel letztes Jahr, tomorrow passt nicht.
wrong.en: There is an error: the statement was made last year, tomorrow does not fit.

wrong.de: Der Fehler liegt bei „tomorrow“: Die Zeitangabe rückt vom Sagen aus mit.
wrong.en: The error is in “tomorrow”: the time word shifts from the speaking.

prompt: Last month Dana wrote that the audit had started yesterday and was still running.
fixed: Last month Dana wrote that the audit had started the day before and was still running.

ok.de: Der Fehler: yesterday zählt von heute. Vom Schreiben aus: the day before.
ok.en: The error: yesterday counts from today. From the writing: the day before.

wrong.de: Doch, hier ist ein Fehler: Dana schrieb letzten Monat, yesterday passt nicht.
wrong.en: There is an error: Dana wrote last month, yesterday does not fit.

wrong.de: Der Fehler liegt bei „yesterday“: Die Zeitangabe rückt vom Schreiben aus mit.
wrong.en: The error is in “yesterday”: the time word shifts from the writing.

a: She said she had called the day before.
b: She said she would call the following day.

q.de: Welcher Satz sagt, dass der Anruf schon vor ihrer Aussage stattfand?
q.en: Which sentence says the call happened before she spoke?

ok.de: Richtig: Satz a. the day before zeigt zurück, vor das Sagen.
ok.en: Right: sentence a. the day before points back, to before the speaking.

wrong.de: In b zeigt the following day nach vorn: Der Anruf kommt erst noch.
wrong.en: In b, the following day points ahead: the call is still to come.

wrong.de: Nicht gleich: Die beiden Sätze zeigen in entgegengesetzte Richtungen.
wrong.en: Not the same: the two sentences point in opposite directions.

from: “Where is the conference room?” the guest asked.

ok.de: Richtig: where the conference room was: erst das Fragewort, dann Subjekt und Verb, ohne did.
ok.en: Right: where the conference room was: question word, subject, verb, no did.

wrong.de: Das Subjekt steht vor dem Verb: where the conference room was.
wrong.en: The subject comes before the verb: where the conference room was.

wrong.de: Das Subjekt steht vor dem Verb: where the conference room is.
wrong.en: The subject comes before the verb: where the conference room is.

wrong.de: Das Schlüsselwort where muss unverändert in der Lücke stehen.
wrong.en: The key word where must stay unchanged in the gap.

from: “Did you receive my email?” Leon asked.

ok.de: Richtig: whether I had received: Ja/Nein-Frage, kein did, mit Rückschritt.
ok.en: Right: whether I had received: yes/no question, no did, with backshift.

wrong.de: „did I receive“ ist die direkte Frage. Indirekt: whether I had received.
wrong.en: “did I receive” is the direct question. Reported: whether I had received.

wrong.de: „receive“ bleibt in der Gegenwart. Nach asked rückt es zu had received.
wrong.en: “receive” stays in the present. After asked it moves to had received.

wrong.de: Das Schlüsselwort whether muss unverändert in der Lücke stehen.
wrong.en: The key word whether must stay unchanged in the gap.

prompt: She asked me did I attend the kickoff.
fixed: She asked me if I attended the kickoff.

ok.de: Der Fehler: Eine Ja/Nein-Frage braucht if oder whether, kein did.
ok.en: The error: a yes/no question needs if or whether, not did.

wrong.de: Doch, hier ist ein Fehler: did I attend ist noch die direkte Frage.
wrong.en: There is an error: did I attend is still the direct question.

wrong.de: Der Fehler liegt bei „did I attend“: Indirekt steht if I attended.
wrong.en: The error is in “did I attend”: reported, it is if I attended.

prompt: I asked the vendor when will it ship.
fixed: I asked the vendor when it would ship.

ok.de: Der Fehler: Das Subjekt steht vor dem Verb. Richtig: when it would ship.
ok.en: The error: the subject comes before the verb. Correct: when it would ship.

wrong.de: Doch, hier ist ein Fehler: when will it ist die Wortstellung der direkten Frage.
wrong.en: There is an error: when will it is the word order of a direct question.

wrong.de: Der Fehler liegt bei „when will it“: Indirekt: when it would.
wrong.en: The error is in “when will it”: reported, it is when it would.

a: She asked whether we had finished the report.
b: She asked if we had finished the report.

q.en: Which sentences say the same thing?

ok.de: Richtig: beide. whether und if leiten hier dieselbe Ja/Nein-Frage ein.
ok.en: Right: both. whether and if introduce the same yes/no question here.

wrong.de: Nicht nur a: if und whether sagen hier dasselbe.
wrong.en: Not only a: if and whether say the same here.

wrong.de: Nicht nur b: whether und if sagen hier dasselbe.
wrong.en: Not only b: whether and if say the same here.

from: “The invoice is overdue,” Maria told the client.

ok.de: Richtig: told the client: tell braucht die Person gleich danach.
ok.en: Right: told the client: tell needs the person right after it.

wrong.de: Nach told steht die Person: told the client.
wrong.en: After told comes the person: told the client.

wrong.de: Das Schlüsselwort told muss unverändert in der Lücke stehen.
wrong.en: The key word told must stay unchanged in the gap.

from: “I'll be late,” Sam said to me.

ok.de: Richtig: said he. say steht ohne Person, mit Person heißt es said to me.
ok.en: Right: said he. say has no person; with one it is said to me.

wrong.de: „said me“ gibt es nicht: Mit Person heißt es said to me.
wrong.en: “said me” does not exist: with a person it is said to me.

wrong.de: Das Schlüsselwort said muss unverändert in der Lücke stehen.
wrong.en: The key word said must stay unchanged in the gap.

prompt: The CFO said the whole team that the budget had been cut.
fixed: The CFO told the whole team that the budget had been cut.

ok.de: Der Fehler: said steht ohne Person. Richtig: told the whole team.
ok.en: The error: said has no person. Correct: told the whole team.

wrong.de: Doch, hier ist ein Fehler: said verträgt keine Person direkt danach.
wrong.en: There is an error: said cannot take a person right after it.

wrong.de: Der Fehler liegt bei „said the whole team“: Mit Person heißt es told.
wrong.en: The error is in “said the whole team”: with a person it is told.

prompt: Our lawyer told us that the contract needed a second signature.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: told us nennt die Person, und needed ist der richtige Rückschritt.
ok.en: No error: told us names the person, and needed is the right backshift.

wrong.de: Kein Fehler: told + Person + that ist hier richtig.
wrong.en: No error: told + person + that is correct here.

a: He told us that the system was down.
b: He said that the system was down.

q.de: Welcher Satz sagt, wem er es gesagt hat?
q.en: Which sentence says who he told?

ok.de: Richtig: Satz a. told us nennt den Empfänger der Nachricht.
ok.en: Right: sentence a. told us names who received the message.

wrong.de: In b fehlt die Person: said that nennt keinen Empfänger.
wrong.en: In b, the person is missing: said that names no recipient.

wrong.de: Nicht gleich: Nur told us nennt den Empfänger.
wrong.en: Not the same: only told us names the recipient.

from: “Please send the draft by Friday,” Elena said to us.

ok.de: Richtig: asked us to send: Eine Bitte ist ask + Person + to + Grundform.
ok.en: Right: asked us to send: request = ask + person + to + base form.

wrong.de: Nach asked us steht to + Grundform, kein -ing.
wrong.en: After asked us use to + base form, not -ing.

wrong.de: Bitten gibt man mit to + Grundform weiter, nicht mit that.
wrong.en: Requests are passed on with to + base form, not with that.

wrong.de: Es fehlt das to: asked us to send.
wrong.en: to is missing: asked us to send.

wrong.de: Das Schlüsselwort asked muss unverändert in der Lücke stehen.
wrong.en: The key word asked must stay unchanged in the gap.

from: “Don't share the file with anyone,” Mr. Park told me.
frame: Mr. Park told me ___ the file with anyone.

ok.de: Richtig: not to share: Die verneinte Anweisung braucht not to + Grundform.
ok.en: Right: not to share: a negative instruction needs not to + base form.

wrong.de: „don't share“ ist der Befehl der direkten Rede. Indirekt: not to share.
wrong.en: “don't share” is the command of direct speech. Reported: not to share.

wrong.de: Das Schlüsselwort not muss unverändert in der Lücke stehen.
wrong.en: The key word not must stay unchanged in the gap.

prompt: My manager asked me sending the slides before the call.
fixed: My manager asked me to send the slides before the call.

ok.de: Der Fehler: Nach asked me steht to + Grundform, kein -ing.
ok.en: The error: after asked me use to + base form, not -ing.

wrong.de: Doch, hier ist ein Fehler: Nach asked me steht kein -ing.
wrong.en: There is an error: no -ing follows asked me.

wrong.de: Der Fehler liegt bei „sending“: Eine Bitte braucht to + Grundform.
wrong.en: The error is in “sending”: a request needs to + base form.

prompt: The client told us not to share the prototype with anyone.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: told us not to share ist die richtige verneinte Anweisung.
ok.en: No error: told us not to share is the correct negative instruction.

wrong.de: Kein Fehler: not to + Grundform ist hier richtig.
wrong.en: No error: not to + base form is correct here.

a: She told me to call him.
b: She told me not to call him.

ok.de: Richtig: Satz b. not to dreht die Anweisung um: Ich soll nicht anrufen.
ok.en: Right: sentence b. not to reverses the instruction: I should not call.

wrong.de: In a steht to call: Ich soll anrufen.
wrong.en: In a, to call: I should call him.

wrong.de: Nicht gleich: not to dreht die Anweisung um.
wrong.en: Not the same: not to reverses the instruction.
